excerpt: Calculate the total cost of buying an Abu Dhabi apartment using DARI service information and the agreed allocation of fees.
introduction:
The cost of an Abu Dhabi apartment includes the agreed price and transaction, financing and setup costs. The amount payable by the buyer depends on the service, agreement and property, so obtain a current itemised quote before committing. A mortgage changes when and how the price is funded; it does not eliminate the purchase cost.

The example below uses a stated fee allocation and sample brokerage, bank and repair costs. The example shows how to organise the purchase price, transaction costs and reserve for an apartment.
takeaways: DARI's listed sale service shows 2% registration on contract value and AED 875 electronic service fee; verify current applicability.
Confirm which party pays each charge under the agreement and include brokerage, finance and initial work.
Budget for service charges, insurance and a separate reserve after purchase.

sections.heading: Which registration fees are listed?
sections.body:
DARI's [sale and purchase registration service](https://services.dari.ae/consumer-services/registration-of-sale-and-purchase-of-land-and-real-estate/) lists a real estate registration fee of 2% of the contract value and an AED 875 electronic service fee for that service. It also lists mortgage-related items where applicable. Check the current service, property type and actual quote; other transactions or channels may differ.

[ADREC's registration legislation](https://adrec.gov.ae/en/rules_and_regulations/registration) describes a sale fee shared equally between buyer and seller unless otherwise agreed under the stated framework. Do not assume the buyer automatically pays the full 2%. Ask the parties and registrar for the agreed allocation and written figures.

Add brokerage and any tax on services, valuation, lender charges, insurance, inspection and initial repairs. Confirm which costs are refundable or included in the price.

sections.heading: Calculate a sample buyer budget
sections.body:
Assume a sample AED 1,000,000 purchase. At the 2% transaction rate listed for DARI's stated service, the total registration amount would be AED 20,000. If the parties agree to share it equally, the buyer's assumed share is AED 10,000. This allocation is an example; confirm your actual agreement and quote.

Add the listed AED 875 electronic service fee, assuming the buyer pays it, plus sample brokerage of AED 22,000, bank costs of AED 8,000 and initial repairs of AED 10,000. The buyer's example total is AED 1,050,875 before a separate reserve, insurance and other possible charges.

The chart shows those components. The sample brokerage, bank and repair amounts are not official rates or quotes. If a mortgage is used, separate the financed portion and repayment schedule from the total cost.

sections.heading: What changes with a mortgage?
sections.body:
Ask the bank for a written offer showing the loan amount, valuation, down payment, interest or profit rate, fees, insurance, repayment dates and early-settlement terms. Approval depends on the applicant and property. If the valuation or approved loan is lower than expected, the buyer may need more cash.

DARI lists mortgage registration and release-related items for the stated sale service, but the amount and application depend on the transaction. Obtain one current quote and avoid adding overlapping service charges twice.

Record the deposit, bank disbursement and transfer date on a calendar. A deposit credited towards the purchase price should not be counted twice. Keep a reserve for repayments and unexpected repairs.

sections.heading: Verify the right and the property
sections.body:
Confirm with ADREC or the relevant registrar that the buyer can acquire the specified right in the exact unit. ADREC's legislation describes non-national rights in investment areas, subject to the applicable framework. The [expat buying guide](/journal/how-to-buy-property-in-abu-dhabi-as-an-expat) explains the documents and questions.

Check title or initial registration, seller authority, any mortgage or tenancy, developer clearance and outstanding service charges. Inspect the actual apartment and shared areas or arrange a qualified inspection. For off-plan, verify the project, payment recipient, instalments and handover provisions.

Do not treat a reservation receipt, rendering or advertisement as the final registration document. Retain the signed agreement and receipts.

sections.heading: Budget for ownership after transfer
sections.body:
Request the unit's current service-charge statement, payment schedule and what it covers. Include utilities, insurance, maintenance and repairs inside the apartment. If it will be rented, add vacancy and management; if it is a family home, consider school and commute costs.

A quoted charge for an unfinished building may be an estimate, not a fixed lifetime amount. Ask when an approved budget will be available and update the calculation. The [Abu Dhabi area guide](/journal/abu-dhabi-real-estate-2026) provides location context, while the building's own documents determine the costs.

Test an unexpected repair or a change in income and keep cash separate from mandatory payments.

sections.heading: Compare ready and off-plan schedules
sections.body:
A ready home may require the balance and transfer costs sooner; an off-plan contract may spread the price across construction and handover. Map every date and include current housing costs until the unit is available. Ask about delays, cancellation and resale in the signed agreement.

Do not compare only the first deposit. An apparently affordable instalment can be followed by a large handover balance. Verify the payment recipient and registration process with the developer and authority. Request a written schedule of any charges payable at each milestone, and check whether a fee contribution is conditional on the contract or a particular payment date.

sections.heading: Request an itemised current quote
sections.body:
Browse the [Aliyas Abu Dhabi project collection](/projects?emirate=Abu%20Dhabi) and [contact Aliyas](/contact) with your budget and financing plans. Ask which exact units are currently available and request the price, payment schedule and cost breakdown. Keep the date and source of every quote so the budget can be updated.

Confirm the current DARI and lender requirements and the agreed fee allocation before paying.
